- **Soap** [`soap`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soap.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Hard olive-oil soap from Venice, the Adriatic coast and Spain is traded; soft lye soap is made at home. Used for laundry and wool scouring, not for medicine. Local: wool scourers of the Arte della Lana; apothecaries.
- **Distillation of strong alcohol (aqua vitae)** [`distillation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/distillation.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Aqua vitae is made by apothecaries and monasteries as a medicine and is recommended against plague. Strength varies; repeated distillation gives spirit that burns. Local: Taddeo Alderotti's consilia (Bologna, d. 1295); monasteries; Arte dei Medici e Speziali.
- **Sulphuric acid (oil of vitriol)** [`sulphuric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sulphuric_acid.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The Latin Geber texts describe distilling vitriol; few alchemists do it, in small weak batches. Vitriol and sulphur are local. Glass and clay vessels crack. Local: alchemists; vitriol and sulphur from the Colline Metallifere and Volterra district.
- **Oxygen and combustion** [`oxygen_combustion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oxygen_combustion.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Fire is an element. Demonstration (candle under a glass over water) is easy, explaining it is hard. Isolating the gas needs mercury calx or saltpetre and gas handling.
- **Nitric acid (aqua fortis)** [`nitric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitric_acid.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. The recipe is some fifty years old (Latin Geber). Mint and goldsmiths still part gold by salt cementation. Saltpetre is scarce and dear; glass and clay retorts break often. Local: Zecca (mint); goldsmiths of Por Santa Maria; alchemists.
- **Saltpetre from nitre beds** [`saltpetre_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/saltpetre_production.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Saltpetre is an imported apothecary and alchemist's salt, also scraped from stable and cellar walls. Demand is small; guns are a novelty. Nitre beds exist nowhere in Europe. Local: apothecaries; the commune's makers of cannon and powder (first ordered 1326). Elsewhere: China and India, saltpetre from nitrous earths.
- **Chemical elements and conservation of mass** [`chemical_elements`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chemical_elements.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Four elements; metals grow from sulphur and mercury, so transmutation is plausible. Assayers have good balances and already rely on weight in practice. Local: assayers of the Zecca.
- **Atomic theory and fixed proportions** [`atomic_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomic_theory.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Atoms are known only through Aristotle's refutation; Lucretius is lost. Atomism threatens the doctrine of the Eucharist. Proof by weight ratios needs pure reagents. Elsewhere: Paris, Nicholas of Autrecourt made to burn his atomist writings (1347).
- **Molecules, Avogadro's hypothesis and chemical formulae** [`molecules_mole_concept`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/molecules_mole_concept.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Periodic table of the elements** [`periodic_table`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/periodic_table.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Only about a dozen of the elements are known as substances here, and none as elements. A table from memory would be unverifiable.
- **Gas laws (pressure, volume, temperature)** [`gas_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_laws.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Scholastics debate whether air has weight and deny the vacuum. Measuring pressure against volume needs a sealed glass tube, much mercury and the idea of air pressure.
- **Collecting and telling apart gases (hydrogen, fixed air)** [`pneumatic_chemistry_gases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pneumatic_chemistry_gases.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Different airs are not imagined; fumes are 'spirits' or corrupted air. Miners know choke-damp. Bladders, glass flasks, a water trough and vinegar are at hand; strong acids are scarce.
- **Acids, alkalis and indicators** [`acids_bases_ph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/acids_bases_ph.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Dyers know that lye and stale urine turn orchil purple and sour liquors redden it. No general concept of neutralising. Local: Rucellai (Oricellari) family, orchil dyers; dyers (tintori).
- **Hydrochloric acid and aqua regia** [`hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Aqua fortis sharpened with sal ammoniac to dissolve gold is in the Latin Geber texts; few have made it. Spirit of salt by itself is unknown. Local: goldsmiths; alchemists.
- **Alkalis (potash, soda, caustic lye)** [`alkali_soda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alkali_soda.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Soda ash from Syria and Egypt feeds glass and soap; wood-ash lye is in every laundry and dye shop. Soda and potash are not told apart. Elsewhere: Syria and Egypt, plant ash exports through Venice.
- **Lime burning and lime mortar** [`lime_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lime_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Quicklime is cheap and plentiful from the building trade. Liming graves and cesspits is practicable and fits the fear of stench. Local: lime kilns supplying the cathedral and wall works.
- **Salt making (sea salt, brine boiling, rock salt)** [`salt_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/salt_production.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The commune sells salt under a hated tax (gabella del sale). Brine is boiled at Volterra; sea salt comes from coastal pans held by Pisa and Siena. Local: Volterra salt springs (moie); salt pans of the Pisan coast and the Maremma.
- **Dyeing with mordants and vat dyes** [`mordant_dyeing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mordant_dyeing.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Dyers use alum with madder, kermes and brazilwood; woad is a vat dye. Alum comes from Phocaea through the Genoese, who took Chios and Phocaea in 1346. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte di Calimala; Arte di Por Santa Maria (silk); dyers (tintori), subordinate to the wool guild. Elsewhere: Phocaea (Asia Minor), alum; Lombardy and the upper Tiber valley, woad.
- **Chlorine, bleaching powder and disinfection** [`chlorine_bleach`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chlorine_bleach.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Linen is bleached with lye, sour milk and sun. Chlorine needs spirit of salt, which nobody makes, plus the manganese glassmakers use. The gas maims.
- **Electrolysis and electroplating** [`electrolysis`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electrolysis.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Needs a battery, and batteries are weak without zinc. Gilders would want plating: it replaces deadly mercury gilding.
